items.title: Nps e "cocaina rosa": cosa c'è nei nuovi mix
items.summary: Nps e "cocaina rosa": cosa c'è nei nuovi mix
items.content:
Cala la diffusione di cannabis ed eroina, così come l'uso di droghe per via endovenosa, la più pericolosa fra le modalità di somministrazione. Ma fra i tanti dati della Relazione annuale al Parlamento sul fenomeno delle dipendenze in Italia - curata dal Dipartimento delle politiche contro la droga e le altre dipendenze, e presentata a fine giugno - le buone notizie finiscono qui. Perché il consumo di droga nel nostro Paese continua a essere elevato.
E perché particolarmente allarmanti sono i dati che riguardano gli adolescenti: il 26% dei 15-19enni ha consumato almeno una sostanza psicoattiva nel 2025, e il 39% l'ha fatto nel corso della vita. Spesso si inizia già a 14 anni, il più delle volte con la cannabis (che resta comunque la droga più usata, nonostante il calo) o con la cocaina, che nelle analisi sulla qualità dell'aria è risultata presente nel 100% dei campioni esaminati. Meno di frequente l'esordio è a base di stimolanti, allucinogeni o altre molecole incluse nella grande famiglia delle nuove sostanze psicoattive (Nps, dall'inglese New psychoactive substances). Queste ultime però guadagnano rapidamente terreno e sono ormai consumate da un ragazzo su 10.. Non a caso, proprio alle Nps è attribuita l'inversione di tendenza dei consumi di droghe, fotografata dal rapporto. «Dopo la flessione osservata tra il 2022 e il 2024, l'andamento appare in aumento», scrivono gli esperti. «Questo incremento è da imputare, principalmente, a una maggior diffusione di stimolanti, cocaina, nuove sostanze psicoattive, oppiacei e oppioidi».. Migliaia di nuove molecole
«Per l'Agenzia antidroga europea (Euda), le nuove sostanze psicoattive sono tutte quelle molecole che compaiono sul mercato ma non sono soggette a controlli, perché non sono incluse nelle tabelle delle sostanze stupefacenti», spiega Carlo Locatelli, direttore del Centro antiveleni dell'Irccs Maugeri di Pavia. L'ultima Relazione europea sulla droga, uscita a inizio giugno, ne individua 1.050, «ma probabilmente ne circolano molte altre che non sono ancora note», spiega l'esperto.
Le più diffuse fra i giovani in Italia sono i cannabinoidi sintetici e semi-sintetici (provati dal 3,6% dei ragazzi), gli oppioidi sintetici (dall'1,6%) e le ketamine (dall'1,2%). «Queste ultime (una sessantina di molecole derivate dalla ketamina) sono anche fra le sostanze che più preoccupano per effetti e potenza, assieme ai catinoni sintetici, e ai fentanili, ottenuti dal fentanyl».. Stop al Fentanyl
Proprio il fentanyl è stato al centro delle cronache per il maxi-furto, avvenuto all'Ospedale israelitico di Roma, di 80 fiale del farmaco, sufficienti a produrre 20.000 dosi. Il fatto che l'episodio si sia verificato proprio in Italia ha il sapore di una beffa, perché il nostro Paese è stato il primo in Europa ad approvare, già nel 2024, un piano ad hoc per contrastare la diffusione di fentanyl e altri oppioidi sintetici, prevedendo un potenziamento del monitoraggio e della prevenzione, oltre che delle capacità dei laboratori di analisi specializzati nell'individuazione di sostanze stupefacenti. Al momento in cui scriviamo, le indagini sono ancora in corso e gli autori del furto ignoti.. Al di là di questa vicenda, tuttavia, i dati dei rapporti europeo e italiano, fermi al 2025, dicono che il fentanyl (che fra il 2020 e il 2024 ha causato circa 120.000 morti per overdose negli Usa) ha ancora una diffusione limitata nell'UE, e che i Paesi più vulnerabili sono quelli Baltici, la Germania e la Bulgaria, che nel 2025 è stata teatro del sequestro di svariati chilogrammi.
Il fentanyl disponibile in Europa deriva da farmaci distratti dal mercato legale (come nel caso romano), oppure è prodotto illegalmente: sequestri di precursori della sostanza sono stati effettuati in Spagna e Olanda, ma non si sa dove fossero destinati. In Italia, 5 decessi sono stati collegati a questo stupefacente nel 2025.. Cocktail pericolosi
Ma non è solo la circolazione di sostanze nuove e sempre più potenti a preoccupare. Sia la relazione italiana sia quella europea documentano infatti un aumento dell'abitudine a consumare più droghe contemporaneamente (il cosiddetto policonsumo, che amplifica i rischi per la salute e complica gli interventi medici in caso di emergenza), accanto a una differenziazione delle modalità di somministrazione.
Riguardo a queste ultime, le Nps (ma anche molte delle droghe "classiche") sono ormai disponibili - oltre che in polvere, liquidi e pasticche - anche in "cristalli", preparati per sigarette elettroniche e alcune persino come additivi per alimenti: «Tutte queste modalità si adattano alle caratteristiche e alle preferenze dei consumatori, ma anche le indirizzano», spiega il rapporto europeo.. L'assunzione di più sostanze contemporaneamente, invece, sembra ormai più la norma che l'eccezione: in Europa coinvolge il 96% dei consumatori di cocaina, il 91% dei consumatori di amfetamina e l'87% di chi usa metamfetamina. Mentre in Italia, il 57% dei nuovi utenti dei Ser.D (i Servizi pubblici per le dipendenze) presi in carico per il consumo primario di cocaina fa uso anche di svariate altre sostanze. Lungo lo stivale, le associazioni che si riscontrano più spesso comprendono cocaina, cannabinoidi e alcol, ma fra gli adolescenti le combinazioni preferite contengono cannabis, Nps (soprattutto cannabinoidi sintetici), stimolanti allucinogeni e cocaina.. La "cocaina" rosa
«A complicare il quadro c'è il fatto che spesso i ragazzi non hanno la più pallida idea di quale droga hanno assunto», interviene Locatelli. «Alcune combinazioni contengono sostanze diverse da quelle dichiarate, oppure del tutto ignote. Gli acquirenti spesso neppure si chiedono che cosa stanno prendendo».
La cosiddetta "cocaina rosa" è un chiaro esempio di questa preoccupante tendenza: «inizialmente conteneva una molecola nota come 2Cb, ancora più costosa della cocaina, con effetto allucinogeno. Ora questa sostanza non è quasi più presente, ma nella polvere rosa può esserci di tutto», dice l'esperto. L'analisi delle partite provenienti da sequestri hanno documentato: ketamina, ecstasy, benzodiazepine, anfetamine, psichedelici, ossicodone (un oppioide) e altro ancora.. Inquinati dalla droga
Ma l'affermazione delle nuove droghe non ha scalzato le vecchie. A documentarlo sono i risultati dei monitoraggi ambientali, che in Italia sono condotti con due modalità: l'analisi delle acque reflue, utilizzata già da vari anni e coordinata dall'Istituto Mario Negri di Milano, e il più recente monitoraggio del PM10.. L'analisi delle acque reflue si basa sulla ricerca delle molecole che derivano dal metabolismo delle sostanze stupefacenti, negli impianti di depurazione. Nel 2025 sono state monitorate 38 città e i risultati confermano che la cannabis resta la droga più utilizzata (con 45 dosi ogni 1.000 abitanti, in calo rispetto agli anni precedenti) seguita dalla cocaina, che fa registrare circa 11 dosi ogni 1.000 abitanti, con un trend costante. Quantità molto inferiori si riscontrano per amfetamine ed ecstasy, ma quest'ultima tende ad aumentare negli anni, così come la ketamina, mentre l'eroina è in diminuzione in tutte le città monitorate..

items.title: “Vuole fare l’amore, ma io le faccio la valigia”
items.summary: Due giorni nella vita di due persone innamorate. Il primo, quando tutto comincia, e l’ultimo, quando ci si lascia. In questa puntata: Paul, 30 anni Leggi
items.content:
Due giorni nella vita di due persone innamorate. Il primo, quando tutto comincia, e l’ultimo, quando ci si lascia. A chi legge, la possibilità di immaginare cosa è successo in mezzo. In questa puntata: : Paul, 30 anni.

“Era l’epoca in cui Tinder era completamente gratuito e io mettevo like a tutti i profili senza pensarci troppo, in piena modalità rimorchio. Per quanto riguarda le mie foto, ho un profilo orientato al marketing: mi si vede sullo skate, vestito da medico o su una scogliera con lo sguardo da amante della natura. Sotto ci scrivo sempre frasi un po’ assurde, come ‘in rivolta permanente’ o ‘il cassetto è nella chiave’, che fanno più intellettuale che medico. Un giorno faccio match con una bellissima ragazza bionda dal viso d’angelo. Sulla sua prima foto abbraccia un gatto così forte da strangolarlo. In un’altra, posa come una modella. Nella biografia cita scrittori russi.

È lei che mi contatta per prima, cosa rara per una ragazza. All’improvviso mi dice che ha voglia di incontrarmi perché sta scrivendo un articolo sulle persone che rimorchiano su Tinder. Cerco su internet, capisco che ha davvero una fanzine di moda. Passiamo due settimane a parlare di letteratura, di arte, comincio a essere preso da questa giovane ragazza super intelligente, che mi ha divertito, mentre di solito mi annoio, anche perché in ospedale non si parla d’altro che del tempo che fa e delle sbronze con gli amici.

Alla fine decidiamo di incontrarci per una mostra al Museo d’arte moderna di Strasburgo. Andavo quasi tutti i giorni a fare skate con i miei amici sul piazzale davanti al museo. Quando arriva, sono tutti curiosi quanto me di vedere com’è. E in effetti è molto bella, non mi sorride, mi analizza, rimane sulla difensiva.

A corto di banalità, usciamo dal museo guardandoci negli occhi come due liceali. A dire il vero, lei va ancora al liceo. Ci sediamo su una panchina del quartiere della Petite France e comincia a piovere come nei film. La gente corre in tutte le direzioni, gli impiegati si coprono la testa con le loro valigette. Le prendo la mano, poi ci baciamo per dieci minuti.

Sull’app Note del mio iPhone ho un elenco delle ragazze con cui vado a letto. A volte non so neanche come si chiamano, in quel caso scrivo ‘ragazza della scala’ o ‘dentro l’ascensore’. Ma sto cambiando le mie abitudini. Le faccio una proposta piuttosto classica, un tè a casa mia – di solito il tè funziona bene, dà l’impressione di un ragazzo rassicurante, che legge libri mentre sorseggia una bevanda calda. L’acqua si riscalda, ma non abbiamo il tempo di metterci dentro la bustina. Dopo lei torna a casa, dai genitori che la aspettano. La vedo andare via e penso che questa volta è una cosa importante. Che mi avrebbe tirato fuori quel ‘ti amo’ che non riuscivo a dire”.

“Gare de l’Est a Parigi, sono parcheggiato in seconda fila, sono venuto a prenderla per portarla in Bretagna. Arriva con degli occhiali da sole che le coprono tutto il viso e lasciano fuori solo le labbra dipinte di rosso vivo. Con un’aria da modella di cattivo umore, appena metto la valigia nel bagagliaio mi accusa di non essere abbastanza contento di vederla. In realtà ho il mio solito atteggiamento indolente. Lei cerca subito lo scontro.

Non apre bocca per tutto il viaggio in autostrada, fino al cartello che indica Chartres. Le propongo di andare a vedere la cattedrale. Da quando vado in vacanza a Saint-Brieuc, non mi sono mai fermato a visitarla. Entriamo in città, mentre parcheggiamo lei trova un capello biondo sul sedile. Mi fa una scenata di gelosia anche se, questa volta, il capello è di mia madre. Furiosa, sbatte la porta e si incammina per Chartres con la sua valigia rossa. Le ruote saltellano sul selciato, le corro dietro, la rassicuro, lei prova a credermi. ‘Te lo giuro, è di mia madre’.

Continuiamo a passeggiare per Chartres, la città è carina, le compro un croissant alle mandorle, il suo dolce preferito. Ci rimettiamo in marcia. Al volante le dico delle parole che non penso, la situazione lo richiede. C’è qualcosa di assoluto nel ‘ti amo’, che mi dà fastidio. Di solito preferisco comportarmi da stronzo, almeno non si rimane delusi. Arriviamo a Pléneuf-Val-André. La casa sulla spiaggia fa il suo effetto, ma il clima di fiducia non si ristabilisce. Lei comincia a farmi una scenata dopo l’altra, non mi dà tregua. Una notte la bacio prima di andare a dormire e la trovo brutta, puzza di sigarette e di sudore. Mi chiudo in camera.

Grida in continuazione, non capisco perché sia voluta venire in Bretagna. Bussa più volte alla porta. L’immagino come una strega, la mia anima non la venera più, è una doccia fredda, come la pioggia del primo giorno ma al contrario. Quella notte decido che non voglio più sentir parlare di lei, come se fosse una storia di una notte finita male.

All’alba, dopo la mia notte chiuso in stanza, la trovo addormentata sul divano. La valigia ai suoi piedi, mezza disfatta, come a dire: ‘Vado via, ma tu trattienimi’. Lei si sveglia, si accende una sigaretta e mi lancia un’occhiata. All’improvviso scappa di casa e si mette a correre a piedi nudi sulla spiaggia, interrompendo gli esercizi degli sportivi delle prime ore del giorno. Mi prende le mani, mi dice che mi ama, che se ne andrà. Le dico che sì, deve andare via.

Torniamo a casa e ridiventa più tranquilla, non credo che voglia davvero andarsene. Vuole fare l’amore, ma io le faccio la valigia. Non dice più nulla, saliamo in macchina e andiamo alla stazione. Come gesto di disperazione, fa accostare l’auto e scappa correndo nel campo vicino alla strada – ha corso parecchio quel giorno. La vedo che si nasconde dietro a un cespuglio, prende il telefono e mi chiama. Lo lascio squillare e lei mi lascia un messaggio in cui mi ripete che mi ama.

Ma io non cedo, arriviamo alla stazione di Saint-Brieuc, sono le 10 di mattina e non ho alcuna idea degli orari dei treni. La lascio sul marciapiede accanto ai binari e decido che non mi interessa più niente di quello che le succederà. Lei è là e io provo odio. Ero davvero innamorato di lei”.

Amore che vieni, amore che vai è una serie del quotidiano francese Le Monde che racconta il primo e l’ultimo giorno di una storia d’amore. Qui ci sono tutte le puntate .

Internazionale pubblica ogni settimana una pagina di lettere. Ci piacerebbe sapere cosa pensi di questo articolo. Scrivici a: posta@internazionale.it

items.title: Cinque piccole storie dalle elezioni negli Stati Uniti
items.summary: Il 3 novembre gli statunitensi hanno votato anche per cambiare le regole, limitare l’autorità delle istituzioni e stabilire quanto potere lasciare ai più ricchi Leggi
items.content:
Oltre a scegliere i loro rappresentanti alle elezioni di metà mandato, il 3 novembre negli Stati Uniti i cittadini si sono confrontati su una questione più generale: chi ha il potere di decidere? Hanno votato per cambiare le regole, limitare l’autorità delle istituzioni, difendere il diritto di essere rappresentati o stabilire quanto potere lasciare ai più ricchi.

Il 3 novembre Laura Mitchell era davanti a un seggio elettorale di Columbia, nel Missouri. Faceva campagna per un referendum che avrebbe reso molto più difficile per i parlamentari statali modificare le leggi approvate direttamente dai cittadini. La storia della proposta risale almeno al 2024, quando gli elettori del Missouri avevano votato per aumentare il salario minimo e garantire a molti lavoratori alcuni giorni di malattia retribuiti. Sei mesi dopo, il parlamento controllato dai repubblicani aveva cancellato quest’ultima misura, eliminando anche gli adeguamenti automatici del salario minimo all’inflazione.

Era successo qualcosa di simile con altre iniziative popolari, sull’aborto, sulla legalizzazione della cannabis e su varie questioni sociali. Nel Missouri, come in molti altri stati americani, i cittadini possono proporre direttamente nuove leggi raccogliendo un numero sufficiente di firme. Ma il parlamento può successivamente modificarle o abrogarle.

Per impedire che continuasse a succedere, un’organizzazione chiamata Respect Missouri voters ha promosso un emendamento alla costituzione statale. I volontari hanno raccolto, secondo gli organizzatori, più di 367mila firme. Il segretario di stato repubblicano – la figura che nei singoli stati si occupa di gestire le elezioni – ha provato a impedire che la proposta arrivasse sulla scheda elettorale, ma a settembre la corte suprema del Missouri gli ha dato torto.

Il 3 novembre l’emendamento è stato approvato con circa il 60 per cento dei voti. Per modificare una legge d’iniziativa popolare, d’ora in poi servirà il sostegno di almeno l’80 per cento dei membri di entrambe le camere del parlamento statale e la successiva approvazione degli elettori in un nuovo referendum. Secondo i critici, tra cui la camera di commercio del Missouri, la norma è troppo rigida e renderà difficile correggere anche eventuali errori o conseguenze impreviste delle leggi approvate dai cittadini. Il risultato, inoltre, non ripristina i giorni di malattia retribuiti aboliti nel 2025.

Ma è il secondo voto in pochi mesi con cui gli elettori del Missouri hanno cercato di difendere gli strumenti di democrazia diretta. Ad agosto, più dell’80 per cento aveva respinto una proposta dei repubblicani che avrebbe reso più difficile approvare gli emendamenti costituzionali d’iniziativa popolare. Il Missouri resta uno stato saldamente repubblicano, ma questi due risultati mostrano che molti elettori sono disposti a opporsi anche ai propri rappresentanti quando ritengono che stiano cercando di limitare il loro potere di decidere direttamente.

Nella riserva della Navajo Nation, in Arizona, il problema di alcuni elettori era molto più immediato: riuscire ad arrivare al seggio. Il 22 ottobre una violenta alluvione aveva devastato la zona di Dennehotso, distruggendo case e strade, interrompendo le forniture di acqua ed elettricità e lasciando ampie distese di fango. Era la terza alluvione in un mese.

Il 3 novembre, davanti al centro comunitario usato come seggio elettorale, arrivavano camion con le ruote coperte di fango. Nel parcheggio le persone mangiavano frybread e stufato di montone, una tradizione tra i navajo nei giorni delle elezioni. Alcuni avevano dovuto servirsi di trattori per superare i tratti di strada impraticabili. Una ruspa stava costruendo un percorso provvisorio per raggiungere il centro abitato, mentre volontari e dipendenti della comunità accompagnavano gli elettori ai seggi. Qualcuno aveva guidato per molte ore.

Tra le persone arrivate quel giorno c’era Lilien Begay, 92 anni, accompagnata dalle figlie. Nell’alluvione aveva perso la casa e tutti i documenti d’identità. Sua figlia Vera ha raccontato al giornalista Adam Burke che la madre non aveva mai saltato una votazione. Begay ha parlato in lingua navajo, spiegando quanto fosse sconvolta per quello che era successo.

Quel giorno i navajo votavano anche per scegliere il proprio presidente. La Navajo Nation , il cui territorio si estende tra Arizona, Utah e New Mexico, ha infatti un governo autonomo, con un presidente che guida l’esecutivo, un parlamento di 24 membri e propri tribunali. Può approvare leggi e amministrare servizi, ma la sua sovranità non è assoluta: deve convivere con i poteri del governo federale e, in alcune materie, con quelli degli stati.

I risultati non ancora ufficiali indicano che la nuova presidente sarà Crystalyne Curley , attuale presidente del parlamento navajo e prima donna a conquistare la carica. Ha ottenuto 32.094 voti contro i 30.979 del suo avversario Justin Jones, che ha detto di voler contestare il risultato. L’elezione si è tenuta lo stesso giorno delle elezioni federali e statali, ma è stata organizzata dalle autorità della Navajo Nation, secondo regole proprie.

Una delle questioni su cui Curley dovrà misurare la propria autorità riguarda il trasporto dell’uranio. Dal 2012 una legge navajo lo vieta sul territorio della riserva, ma prevede un’eccezione per le strade statali e federali che lo attraversano. Su quelle strade passano i camion che trasportano il minerale estratto vicino al Grand Canyon verso uno stabilimento nello Utah. Nel 2025 il governo navajo ha raggiunto un accordo con la società mineraria per consentire i trasporti a condizioni più rigorose. Ma le preoccupazioni sono rimaste, anche dopo che a luglio uno dei camion (vuoto) si è ribaltato durante un temporale.

Curley ha promesso che nei primi cento giorni di mandato incaricherà il procuratore generale della Navajo Nation di trovare, insieme alle autorità dell’Arizona, una soluzione legale per fermare il trasporto dell’uranio sulle strade statali che attraversano il territorio navajo.

In Alabama, nel sud degli Stati Uniti, le regole del voto sono state al centro di una battaglia politica. Ma in questo caso a cambiarle sono stati i parlamentari repubblicani, approfittando di una decisione della corte suprema federale.

Pochi giorni prima delle elezioni, il giornalista Zak Cheney-Rice ha incontrato Shomari Figures nel suo quartier generale di Montgomery. Figures è un deputato democratico nero, eletto per la prima volta nel 2024 in un collegio creato dopo una lunga battaglia giudiziaria . In Alabama gli afroamericani rappresentano circa il 27 per cento della popolazione con diritto di voto; per anni le mappe elettorali avevano concentrato una parte degli elettori neri in un solo collegio e disperso gli altri nei restanti sei, riducendo così la loro influenza e lasciandogli la possibilità concreta di eleggere un candidato di propria scelta in un solo collegio su sette. Un tribunale federale aveva giudicato illegale quella distribuzione e imposto una nuova mappa, che aveva permesso a Figures di essere eletto.

Il 29 aprile di quest’anno la corte suprema federale ha però indebolito le tutele contro il ridisegno dei collegi, chiamato gerrymandering . Due giorni dopo, la governatrice repubblicana Kay Ivey ha convocato una sessione straordinaria del parlamento statale, che sotto la guida dei repubblicani ha approvato una nuova mappa , riprendendone una precedentemente respinta dai giudici. La percentuale di popolazione nera nel collegio di Figures è scesa dal 47 al 40 per cento. Sono state escluse anche la contea in cui il deputato è cresciuto e quella dove alcuni suoi antenati erano stati ridotti in schiavitù. Un seggio che due anni prima aveva conquistato con quasi dieci punti di vantaggio era diventato, secondo le previsioni, favorevole ai repubblicani.

Figures ha vinto lo stesso. Ma quando Cheney-Rice lo ha intervistato, dopo le elezioni, ha messo in guardia dal trarre conclusioni troppo ampie. Ha spiegato che i repubblicani avevano avuto poco tempo per rendere il collegio ancora più difficile da conquistare e che probabilmente ci avrebbero riprovato.

C’è un aspetto politico interessante nella candidatura di Figures, che mostra come i candidati democratici abbiano cercato di porsi in modo molto diverso rispetto alle elezioni precedenti: durante la campagna elettorale aveva parlato molto poco del gerrymandering , concentrandosi invece sui problemi quotidiani degli elettori.

Figures sostiene che sarebbe un errore considerare gli afroamericani un gruppo omogeneo, da conquistare parlando esclusivamente di diritti civili e discriminazioni. La sua vittoria ha dimostrato che l’ostacolo di una mappa sfavorevole può essere superato, almeno in un’elezione eccezionalmente favorevole ai democratici. In Tennessee e Louisiana, però, altre modifiche ai collegi hanno già contribuito a ridurre le possibilità di rappresentanza degli elettori neri.

A Perry, un paese di circa 1.400 abitanti nell’Ohio nordorientale, il giorno dopo le elezioni John Nicely stava guidando il suo scuolabus quando alcuni studenti gli hanno chiesto scherzosamente quando avrebbe tolto i cartelli elettorali. Nicely, che ha più di sessant’anni e in passato ha lavorato nel mondo degli affari, era diventato uno dei protagonisti di una mobilitazione contro gli accordi proposti da un’azienda intenzionata a costruire un grande data center nel paese. Il referendum per cui aveva fatto campagna, l’Issue 16, era appena stato approvato con l’87 per cento dei voti.

items.title: Ultorg: The User Interface for Relational Databases
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.ultorg.com/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50435898 Points: 82 # Comments: 23
items.content:
Ultorg is an efficient, spreadsheet-like UI for relational databases. Query and edit data across tables and relationships, without SQL or custom CRUD apps. Watch the conference talk.

@ultorg is the most mind blowing database tool I have ever seen. The way it can visualize multiple joins feels canonical in the sense that now, when I run complicated SQL queries, *that’s* the format I use to imagine the results. vimeo.com/695905306

Jaw dropping talk on a way to view SQL databases without writing a custom app. Imagine Microsoft Access crossed with Microsoft Excel and a big dose of incredible sorcery So exciting!! Can’t wait to learn more about @ultorg

This presentation by @eirikbakke on a generic UI abstraction to navigate a relational database is the most exciting bit of interaction design I've seen in a long, long time. vimeo.com/372006027

The future never came: I expected dynamic multi-dimensional spreadsheet to sooner or later become the norm ever since I saw Lotus Improv. With @ultorg you get to wonder – perhaps the multidimensional UI is to a set of database tables, not to a spreadsheet.

"Harmonic is building mathematical superintelligence. Deep, detailed analysis of our system's outputs is crucial for rapid advancement of our research agenda. Ultorg provides, by far, the best tool for visualizing and investigating our data. It is an invaluable tool for our research." -Tudor Achim, co-founder and CEO, Harmonic Tables of Data Whether in finance, engineering, operations, or the life sciences, you are likely working with tables of data in spreadsheets, CSV files, or an external database. Spreadsheets are excellent tools for managing a single table of data. They are a poor fit for database tasks, however, where data must be combined and queried in many different ways.

Ultorg is a general-purpose, graphical user interface for relational databases . That means any data that's organized into tables with rows and named columns. Behind the scenes, Ultorg generates SQL queries that execute either remotely or on your local computer.

A join is a fundamental database operation that combines data from two different tables, based on a common identifier such as "Room Number" or "Customer ID". Joins are frequently needed when working with multi-table datasets.

In Ultorg, you can quickly join data from multiple tables or data sources, and interact with the result through a single, spreadsheet-like data manipulation surface.

For SQL-based data sources, Ultorg will recognize existing foreign key relationships, and suggest relevant joins. Or you can join on arbitrary fields, e.g., to combine data from a spreadsheet and a CSV file.

A join between two tables will often involve a one-to-many relationship , where each row in the first table can match multiple rows in the second table.

Ultorg will visualize any combination of one-to-many relationships, in a compact but readable way, using a specially developed system of visual data layouts. Sorting, filters, and formulas can be applied at any level, and joins can be chained or included side-by-side without losing or duplicating rows.

Among visual database tools, Ultorg is unique in its ability to handle one-to-many relationships in a general way.

One-to-many relationships also occur inside database queries, when grouping on fields to calculate sums or averages, or when nesting one query within another. Ultorg will visualize each stage of such data flows.

For example, you can see the individual values that contribute to a group-wise sum . This lets you audit the query visually. You can tweak filters and calculations in the input, while gaining confidence in the aggregated totals.

At first glance, Ultorg's direct manipulation interface resembles a spreadsheet. The tabular layout you see on the screen, however, represents a real database query, which can be refreshed and modified without risking changes to the underlying raw data.

A visual query lets you see exactly the data you need for a particular business task, without descending into a code editor, form designer, or flow chart. Even for database experts, Ultorg will serve as a rapid alternative to hand-typed SQL.

Most SELECT queries that can be written in the core SQL language have a visual equivalent in Ultorg. For example, you can express arbitrary combinations of joins, filters, calculations, and subqueries.

In business or engineering data, or in the social sciences, you may be dealing with hundreds of fields of various data types-text, numbers, and dates-spread across dozens of tables, each with thousands (or millions) of rows.

To retain sanity, it is essential not to have to spend time tweaking formatting settings for each individual field, or for every new database query.

Ultorg eliminates such hard, manual labor, by analyzing your data on the fly and deriving carefully tuned defaults. For example, label placements, table column widths, text field dimensions, decimal precision, and pagination are all handled automatically. You can see all your data with fewer keystrokes.

Ultorg's typographical engine can visualize records and one-to-many relationships using a combination of general-purpose strategies, such as nested tables , forms , and crosstabs .

Ultorg's visual data layouts are analogous to the hand-designed user interface screens you might see in traditional, tailored database applications. But in Ultorg, they are available immediately, for any data, without custom programming.

From Ultorg, you can also edit data, stored in a relational database, in a Microsoft Excel workbook, or in Google Sheets .

You can edit values in individual cells, pick values from a dropdown , insert rows, or fill down , like in a spreadsheet. You can review changes before committing to the database. Multiple users can edit at the same time. For internal business operations, Ultorg can serve as an alternative to custom CRUD interfaces, or as a way to supercharge your spreadsheet-based recordkeeping.

Start Ultorg and connect immediately to your data source. No "cloud" required; all data stays private on your computer or corporate network.

just connected @ultorg to the @MusicBrainz database and WOW this thing is cool hytradboi.com/2022/ultorg-a-…

Wow! It is so refreshing to see such a revelation — a work of art in user interfaces! (Warning: no micro-interactions, no gradients.)

This thing blew my mind for how good a SQL admin interface can be. I was pretty happy with metabase until this talk. Wow! Really wow!

This is outstanding work! The trick is how to integrate it with users' workflows. If people can leverage Ultorg without leaving Excel/Salesforce/any CRM/ERP this is massive.

items.title: Formalizing CPython
items.summary: Article URL: https://broyojo.com/python-formalization/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50435105 Points: 83 # Comments: 32
items.content:
AI agents wrote 613,318 lines of Lean that copy Python's internals line by line, tested every piece against the real Python, had a computer check every proof, and turned up 418 bug reports in Python along the way.

Python doesn't have a precise written definition. There is a reference manual, but in practice "Python" means whatever CPython does, and CPython is hundreds of thousands of lines of C plus a large standard library. The manual covers normal use. It says little about the odd cases, and that's where bugs hide: an object that changes a dictionary while that dictionary is searching for it, an error thrown halfway through an update, a number one past the largest the C code was written for.

Writing a proof about a function forces you to say exactly what it does in all of those cases. You can't leave anything vague, because the proof checker won't accept it. That makes proofs a good way to find the places where the code doesn't do what everyone assumes.

We wanted to see how far this goes on a code base as large and old as CPython, and whether the results stay trustworthy when most of the work is done by AI.

The code at the top of this page is step one for a small piece of CPython: the C function that works out how many numbers are in a range , next to its Lean copy. The copy keeps the C code's exact arithmetic, including how its numbers wrap around when they get too big. The proof about it shows that this function, the slower version CPython uses for very large numbers, and the code that chooses between them always give the same, correct count.

The hardest part wasn't getting AI agents to write proofs. It was getting proofs that actually mean something.

Our first attempt asked the agents for breadth: copy every function and prove at least one thing about each. They did. Then a separate review found that fewer than half of the functions it checked held up, and in one file only 21%. The proofs were all correct. They just didn't say anything useful. For example, "if this function returns a number, the number is at least zero" is true, but a function that always crashes also satisfies it.

So the reviewer now asks one question about every proof: could a broken version of the function pass it too?

Fixing a weak proof usually means going back and making the copy more realistic, for example letting a user's code throw an error in the middle of a function. The charts below show how that went for ten files. Each point is one round of review. The lines sometimes go down: when a reviewer finds that an accepted proof is wrong about real Python, everything that relied on it is taken back out.

A checked proof guarantees that a statement follows from the copy. It doesn't guarantee the copy matches real Python, and testing only covers the inputs you thought to try. So every accepted statement is also run against real Python. That caught several proofs that were valid and still wrong.

The copy of Python's fast JSON encoder assumed memory requests always succeed. So it "proved" the encoder could build its indentation strings for any nesting depth, including one that needs 16 terabytes of memory. Real Python runs out of memory. The fixed copy now treats every memory request as something that can fail.

A proof said Python's pickle module never goes deeper than a certain number of nested calls. That turned out true except in a brand-new Python process. There, the first time it encodes a string, it quietly loads a text codec, and that load uses nine more nested calls. Our tests never saw it, because the test harness had already loaded the codec.

In Python, catching a TypeError also catches any more specific error built on top of it. Three separate copies checked an error's exact name instead. All three had proofs that a custom error type could break.

The copy of Python's set assumed that once memory is freed, the same address never comes back. Real memory allocators reuse addresses all the time. CPython uses a "did the address change?" check to notice when user code has swapped out the set's internals. With reuse, that check can be fooled. Fixing the copy turned an accepted proof into a real memory bug, now one of our bug reports.

When a proof fails because Python itself is wrong, and not the copy, we write it up as a bug report. Each report includes a short script that shows the bug on Python 3.15.2 (for most, also on the development version), a search for duplicates already reported, and an honest rating of how much it matters.

Most are small: an error message that's wrong, an edge case that behaves differently from the documentation, two versions of a function that disagree. About 55 are more serious and can crash Python or corrupt its memory using nothing but normal Python code, usually by having user code change a container while C code is in the middle of using it. Python doesn't treat running hostile Python code as a security boundary, so these are ordinary bugs. The ones not already on CPython's tracker are being reported to the project, starting with this post. Six small examples of different kinds:

Calling setdefault on an object's attribute dictionary with a StrEnum key crashes the interpreter, if another object of the same class has that attribute and this one doesn't.

Assigning to a backwards slice of an ElementTree element should insert, as it does for a list. Instead it duplicates one child without taking a reference and loses another.

A Message-ID with a space inside square brackets makes Python's email parser fail with an internal error. The header comes from whoever sent the email.

New in Python 3.15, the base32 decoder can ignore chosen characters. If = is one of them, where it appears still changes the result.

Giving an enum value to a second member should raise an error. If the class's __repr__ is broken, the error is swallowed and the call quietly does nothing.

Python has a C pickler and a pure-Python one. They give up at different nesting depths. This difference was first reported in 2008 and is still open.

None of this is specific to Python. It works for anything with source code you can read and a working version you can run: another language, a library, a file format, a compiler. What made the difference for us:

The instructions our agents worked from are in the repository and meant to be reused: AGENTS.md for the agents doing the work, REVIEW_PROMPT.md for the reviewers, and the full list of functions with their status in coverage/methods .

The closest project is julia-in-lean , which did this for the Julia language and directly inspired this one 1 . It modelled Julia's standard library in Lean, tested the models against Julia, recorded about 400 bugs and filed 75. Its finding that 128 of 130 quick proofs had quietly assumed away the hard case shaped our review rules. A recent paper models NVIDIA's PTX GPU instruction set in Lean to prove GPU kernels correct 2 , building on earlier formal work on PTX's memory model 3 .

For Python specifically, λπ 4 and a K framework semantics of Python 3.3 5 described the language mathematically; this project copies CPython's actual code instead. Similar efforts exist for JavaScript 6 , 7 and WebAssembly 8 , and CompCert 9 and seL4 10 remain the high bar for fully verified software. Comparing two implementations on the same inputs, the testing half of this project, goes back decades 11 , 12 .

The project started on 29 October 2026. 4,071 of the 26,004 functions worth checking (15.7%) have been copied, tested, proved and accepted by review. The Lean code is 613,318 lines in 1,539 files, containing 18,898 theorems and lemmas; 3,834 of the top-level properties are proved and 588 are proved false with a counterexample. Most of Python is still ahead, especially the large part of the standard library written in Python itself. Multithreading is out of scope for now. In these 57 files, every function copied so far has passed review. The 30 with the most accepted functions:

The project is open, and help is welcome. Most of CPython is still unmodelled: pick a file whose functions are still marked todo in coverage/methods , follow AGENTS.md , and send a pull request. Independent reviews of existing work count as much as new models. See CONTRIBUTING.md .

items.title: Qantas to outsource 850 local jobs with most roles moving to India
items.summary: The Australian airline said the move was aimed at modernising its IT systems and noted the impact of AI.
items.content:
Qantas will outsource 850 local corporate jobs to consulting giant Accenture with most roles moving to India as the airline fast-tracks AI investment.

In an internal email to staff on Tuesday, the Australian company's CEO Vanessa Hudson said "this is hard news for some and I'm sorry for the uncertainty it brings".

The job cuts will begin mid-2027, she said, and start with finance, procurement, people and marketing roles shifting "mostly" to teams in India and "some in Australia" as the firm seeks to modernise its IT systems.

Hudson said the "scale and speed of change in technology and AI is something none of us has seen in our lifetime", and it was in talks with unions and staff on the plans.

The move comes days after the airline provided a market update, flagging fare increases and flight cuts amid higher fuel costs.

On its new multi-year deal with Accenture, Hudson said it was about "modernising" the airline's IT systems to become "more efficient".

Qantas spends more than AU$1bn (US$691m; £514m) a year on technology, she said, and the company's back-end systems needed to be upgraded.

"Like every airline, we run on technology built up over decades for a different era, including more than 1,000 legacy applications that were never designed to work together," she said.

The deal with Accenture means "we will redesign and simplify parts of how our corporate functions work and reduce duplication", Hudson said, so staff can "spend more time on work that creates value for our customers and the business".

The company said that "in time", the work that Accenture takes over will be "transformed further with automation and AI".

Staff affected by the job cuts will be redeployed "where possible", the firm added, including new roles in Australia.

Qantas - which employs about 28,000 staff in Australia and another 4,000 globally - said thousands of its staff already use AI in their daily work.

The BBC has contacted the Australian Services Union for comment.

items.title: 'Cruise for life' ship seized in Singapore
items.summary: The Odyssey was meant to take guests around the world for years, but the trip was cut short after its operator ran out of money.
items.content:
A round-the-world cruise that left passengers stranded in Cambodia after its US-based operator ran out of money has been seized in Singapore.

The Odyssey, which set off from Belfast in October 2024 and was meant to take guests on a years-long voyage around the world, is now anchored in Singapore port waters, local authorities say.

Around 200 guests were forced to leave the ship last month in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, after its owner Villa Vie Residences abruptly suspended operations citing "extraordinary increases in fuel costs".

The crew onboard are reported to be well, Singapore's port authority said.

"Arrangements for their welfare and wellbeing are being managed by the vessel's creditors," the authority said, adding that the vessel had been "placed under arrest pursuant to a court order".

Singapore law firm Helmsman LLC has been named the "arresting solicitor", but it is not clear which party it represents.

The Odyssey was meant to go on a three-and-a-half-years voyage covering 150 countries.

Passengers were given the options of buying their cabin outright, which allows them to stay onboard beyond its initial voyage, paying for a five-year residency, or renting a cabin for days-long tours.

Permanent residencies in its cabins ranged from $120,000 (£89,272) to $440,000. Those cabins were also available for rent from $3,500 a month, according to its website.

"For roughly the price of a car, you can own your home on a ship that travels the world," its founder Mikael Petterson had earlier said.

However the cruise was beset with problems from the start, with its departure delayed for four months because of repairs and paperwork.

While in Vietnam, crew members reportedly bought food from local grocery stores because the company owed money to a vendor who refused to deliver food, according to CBS News, the BBC's partner in the US.

CBS also reported that the operator warned passengers of its financial troubles in August, when it had sailed on a separate occasion into Singapore, and had to raise money from guests to keep the cruise going.

Holly Hennessey, one of the ship's passengers, had earlier told the BBC guests were asked to consider paying a fuel surcharge as prices soared, and that their itinerary had been "severely curtailed".

The vessel sailed again into Singapore earlier this month, weeks after the cruise came to a sudden end while in Cambodia.

As the Iran war sent fuel prices soaring earlier this year, monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia had risen to as much as $8,000 from $1,800, Villa Vie Residences said in a statement on 27 October.

It added that it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption" but those measures turned out to be insufficient to offset the "extraordinary increase in fuel costs".

The company also said it was working with residents to "identify temporary living arrangements" while in Cambodia.

Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs

items.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
items.summary: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.
items.content:
A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution.

"By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said.

The effort will likely fail, as Republicans remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says the effort is aimed at pushing President Donald Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.

Hegseth has called the impeachment effort a "sham" and defended his record.

"You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said in a video statement last week. "It's not going to work. We will not back down."

He called Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" and said he was not concerned about the impeachment effort. In the video, Hegseth defended his leadership of the department and listed ways he has fulfilled Trump's America First agenda.

Massie formally introduced his articles of impeachment in a resolution on the House floor on Monday afternoon. The move starts a 48-hour clock for the chamber to take up the measure. Lawmakers could vote on the resolution directly, vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside.

"I'm doing this because it's the right thing to do," he told reporters after introducing the articles.

Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it started nearly nine months ago. He has previously garnered headlines over demanding the Trump administration release the files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and has now brought them back in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections.

He has said the effort was aimed at preventing a Democrat spectacle next year when they have control of Congress. He said he hoped to force Trump to name a replacement, who could be quickly confirmed while Republicans have power.

"My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials."

Democratic leadership has signalled openness to such an effort against Hegseth once they take control in January.

Asked about the effort on Monday, Hegseth said, "We're not worried about that".

He said he planned to hold a news conference on Tuesday to discuss the subject.

President Trump has indicated that he plans to stick by Hegseth , praising his leadership in the US capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro earlier this year and defending his work during the war in Iran.

"We've made the world a lot safer place. Why haven't we gone after all these other people that ran wars and lost?" Trump said on Monday at the White House.

"The soldiers, the actual soldiers, the great people that do the work, the great patriots, they love Pete Hegseth," he said. "He's done a very good job."

Impeaching a cabinet secretary is rare. It must be approved by both chambers for the secretary to be removed from office.

Trump was impeached by the House twice in his first term in office but was cleared by the Senate after two trials and not removed.

As with the presidential process, the House would first hold a vote on charges against Hegseth and the Senate then would conduct a trial to decide whether to acquit or convict.

The House has voted to impeach only two cabinet members in US history, but the Senate did not convict either one.

While impeachment has been "an incredibly rare process", it has become far more normalised since the House impeached President Bill Clinton in 1998, said Paul Gowder, a law professor at Northwestern University in Chicago.

He said it has become "much more common as the country has become more politically polarised," adding a prediction that several more of Trump's cabinet members may face impeachment over the next two years.

Massie told reporters he was not sure if the measure had sufficient backing to pass. It would need a majority to pass the House and even with all Democratic support, it would still likely need some Republican support as the party holds a slim majority.

Peter Loge, a professor of public affairs at George Washington University, told the BBC that he believed it was likely to pass due to those slim margins.

"There are enough angry Republicans that more than enough Republicans are gonna simply not show up to vote," he said.

Currently, there are 218 Republicans and 214 Democrats in the House.

While the House requires a simple majority to pass articles of impeachment, the Senate mandates a two-thirds vote to convict, threshold that is difficult to meet in the current congressional term.

When Democrats take over in January, they are likely to have at least 54 Senate seats - though two races do not yet have winners due to slim voting margins. A total of 67 votes will be required to convict and remove an official from office.

- 10/11/2026 - This story was updated to reflect that 67 votes in the Senate are needed to remove an official from office

White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses

items.title: 'There is no justice' - Epstein survivor on how model agency sent her to abuser's home
items.summary: A woman says an agency boss sent her to photoshoots at the sex offender's Florida beach home.
items.content:
A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says the president of the model agency representing her put her in danger, when he sent her to two photoshoots at the convicted sex offender's Florida beach house.

At the time, in 2009, Epstein was serving a jail sentence for sex offences against a minor but was allowed to work each day from his home.

"My agency's job was to protect me, and they failed. In fact, they put me in danger. And for that, they should be held accountable," she tells the BBC World Service.

Roza was 18 when she was first sent to Epstein's Palm Beach home by MC2 Model Management's US branch, having only arrived in the US from Uzbekistan about a month earlier. MC2's US president at the time, Jeff Fuller, now runs another US model agency called The Source Models.

"My agency knew exactly where I was. So Jeff knew exactly where I was going," says Roza.

She shows us an expense statement suggesting Fuller himself booked her flight home from Palm Beach, following her second shoot at Epstein's home. Fuller has previously claimed he did not know Roza was going to Epstein's house.

She says the photoshoots led to her being employed as an assistant to Epstein. Other survivors have explained how the financier used the recruitment of assistants as an elaborate ruse to allow him to continue abusing young women .

Fuller has not responded to the BBC's allegations. He has previously said he did not know Roza was being abused.

We discovered through the Epstein-related documents released by the US Department of Justice [DOJ] that 10 models from MC2 met, or were in communication with, Epstein after his conviction.

The files also show Epstein gave $1m (£742,000) to MC2 in 2005 - despite the agency owners telling a US publication two years later that Epstein had no involvement in their company.

Testimony shared with BBC Eye also raises questions about the role played by two other individuals who were active in the model industry, and whom the DOJ files show had close relationships with Epstein - former agent Ramsey Elkholy and agency director Faith Kates.

A DOJ statement from last year, that no evidence has been uncovered which would warrant further investigation against "uncharged third parties", is now being challenged by New York State senator, Zellnor Myrie.

He has proposed a new sex trafficking bill to give police greater power to investigate Epstein's alleged enablers.

Sara Ziff, founder of the Model Alliance, which campaigns for stronger protections for models in the US, approves.

"Often, [model agencies] are the problem. They are the link between the model and these predatory men."

Roza says the person behind the camera at the photoshoots MC2 sent her to was not a professional photographer, but Epstein's girlfriend at the time, Nadia Marcinko .

Roza describes the set-up as "strange - there was no stylist" and the photos were never used. She has since become convinced the shoots were stage-managed by Epstein and MC2.

BBC Eye reveals new evidence showing how scouts, agencies and powerful fashion figures helped Jeffrey Epstein gain access to young women after his conviction for sex offences.

If you are outside the UK, please watch on YouTube , external

An email in the DOJ files, from Fuller to Epstein, makes clear the close ties between the agency and the financier.

"Had it not been for you, we would have fired her months ago," Fuller writes of another model in March 2012. "And I would be careful as she blabs about things," he says.

A month after Epstein's second arrest in 2019, MC2's US branch was dissolved and Fuller opened a new agency, The Source Models, which is still operating. The BBC has found that 50 models from MC2 were transferred to his new agency.

We asked The Source Models to comment on our findings - it did not reply.

Model agencies were useful to Epstein, says Sigrid McCawley, the lead lawyer for more than 100 of Epstein's victims.

"Epstein said to many people he wanted three different girls a day. Think about those numbers... The [model] scouts were really critical because they were the ones who were identifying the type of woman that Epstein liked."

In the case of former agent Ramsey Elkholy, BBC Eye has discovered he tried to connect 34 women to Epstein, including an 18-year-old who was still in school.

The experience of one of the women highlights how assistants would be co-opted into the structure of the abuse.

Elkholy, the DOJ files show, suggested to Epstein that one of the financier's female assistants befriend this woman, before introducing her to Epstein.

We spoke to this woman, and she revealed that at her first meeting with Epstein, aged 19, he sexually abused her in his New York townhouse.

Ramsey Elkholy told the BBC: "I completely reject any allegation that I knew of or facilitated abuse of any kind… At the time, I had no knowledge of any abuse and I knew only his own [Epstein's] account of his 2008 [legal] case, which I misguidedly believed."

He continued: "The record and published reporting show that women were often groomed by other women in his inner circle. I was never part of that circle, or indeed of any such activity… my intention was to help models find professional opportunities by introducing them to an extremely well-connected individual."

If you are in the UK and you have been affected by any of the issues in this story such as sexual abuse and violence , information and support is available at BBC Action Line

Lawyer Sigrid McCawley says these female assistants would have had "no choice" in how they conducted themselves.

"These young survivors were being abused regularly. Their livelihoods were being threatened… They had to do what they were being told to do."

Another model we have spoken to, Simona (not her real name), from eastern Europe, told us Epstein had raped her more than 200 times.

"People think that we gained something, that we agreed on this abuse in order to gain something, whether it's monetary or influential, but it's not true. We're left with deep trauma," says Simona.

She says the first time she met the financier, aged 20, she was already signed with a model agency in New York, and he offered to introduce her to his "good" friend Faith Kates.

At the time, Kates was the head of Next Management, one of the world's biggest model agencies. She stepped down from that senior executive position in December last year, but is still legally listed as a director of the company.

Simona says at this meeting, Kates suggested she undergo plastic surgery and sent details of a surgeon to Epstein.

After her meeting with Kates, Simona says Epstein convinced her to stop modelling.

And just like Roza, and several other of his victims, she became his assistant. She says he went on to rape her and control every aspect of her life for nearly two years.

The DOJ files show Epstein asked Kates to meet an additional five models, though it is not clear how many of these meetings took place.

Lawyers for Faith Kates told the BBC: "Jeffrey Epstein was a master manipulator... Ms Kates was one of those grossly misled by Epstein. Had she known then what she - and everyone else - now knows, she would have never associated with him."

They added she had never asked a model to have plastic surgery.

We approached Next Management for comment, but it did not reply.

Myrie told the BBC that if his bill were to become law, and "you were sending models to Epstein and you knew what Epstein was doing, or you should have known what he was doing, you will be held accountable".

Roza hopes sharing her story will encourage others to come forward.

"There are many, many survivors out there who never speak, because it's scary. So to all my sister survivors… you know me now. You know my name. I say, reach out."

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep
items.summary: Article URL: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/9/mysterious-beeps/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50434310 Points: 214 # Comments: 95
items.content:
Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven’t unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn’t want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator , a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room.

Here’s what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while:

You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners—I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra.

The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn’t work particularly well, so I added a “Rough mode” where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds.

I added a clapping mode too so I could test it by clapping my hands in different locations around the room—displayed as diamonds on the map. This helped me gain confidence that it was capable of locating a sound.

Beeps show up on the map as an X, plus a line in the “Sounds located” log. You can replay these sounds (from each device in turn) to confirm they are the mysterious beep you are looking for, then click “This is the mystery beep” to mark them as such.

Once you’ve confirmed the mysterious beep frequency the system will listen out for it, measure the interval between beeps, and use the triangulated locations to lock down the most likely location on the map.

The system worked as intended. It gave me the position of the beep to within about 40cm, then I dug through that specific pile of boxes and found an ancient carbon monoxide detector that desperately wanted its batteries replaced.

When I started working through this problem with Claude it quickly dug up BeepBeep: A High-Accuracy Acoustic-Based System for Ranging and Localization Using COTS Devices , a 2007 paper by Chunyi Peng, Guobin Shen, Yongguang Zhang, Yanlin Li, and Kun Tan. Here’s that paper’s abstract:

We present the design, implementation, and evaluation of BeepBeep, a high-accuracy acoustic-based ranging system. It operates in a spontaneous, ad-hoc, and device-to-device context without leveraging any pre-planned infrastructure. It is a pure software-based solution and uses only the most basic set of commodity hardware – a speaker, a microphone, and some form of device-to-device communication – so that it is readily applicable to many low-cost sensor platforms and to most commercial-off-the-shelf mobile devices like cell phones and PDAs. It achieves high accuracy through a combination of three techniques: two-way sensing, self-recording, and sample counting.

Beep Locator runs a Python web application server that does most of the work. The listening devices then connect to that server via WebSockets and present a UI which requests browser microphone access. The listeners mainly work by recording a 60 second buffer of recent audio. They also run a simple beep detection algorithm (see detector.js ), which uses Fast Fourier Transform and a high-pass filter to identify potential beeps. It sends these events to the main server.

When a beep is reported, the server has a device play a short chirp (the device with the lowest round-trip time to the server), then asks every listener upload a clip from about 0.6s before the beep to 0.8s after that chirp. This chirp allows the clips to be aligned with each other, a crucial step in locating the beep.

I started this project using Claude Code Cloud via my iPhone, with Opus 5.5 running in Extra thinking effort mode. Here’s that shared starter session , which began with this prompt against a newly created empty GitHub repository:

Write out a problem.md file describing the problem we want to solve

I want to set up several devices - laptops, phones, iPads - around the room all listening at the same time and have them help triangulate where the beep comes from

There needs to be a Python web app which coordinates it all - one device shows a web page for the app, other devices join a URL which turns them into listeners - all via browser WebAudio and WebSockets back to the Python server app

Ideally I wouldn't need to manually input the relative locations of the devices - it would be amazing if they could play sounds to each other in order to locate each other in 2D space - is that even possible though?

That got me this problem.md file . As part of writing that up Claude found and read the BeepBeep paper, which is described in that file.

Ok try and build it, add a mechanism so you can send new code to the listeners which they will then run automatically - that way I can set everything up in the room and then leave you alone to continue hacking and experiment while I do something else

That got me to this point —most of the system was built, but nothing had actually tried running it yet.

I cloned the new repository to my laptop and fired up Claude Code... and then Fable 5.2 was released , and this project seemed like an excellent opportunity to put that through its paces.

I had Claude Code on my laptop start the server running, then made sure it could both see what was happening and make live changes to the software as it ran.

This was already baked into the software: Opus 5.5 had built an installModule() method on the listeners that could be triggered over the WebSocket connection, meaning the admin server could execute arbitrary new code on any of its clients.

On some devices, web pages that listen on the microphone request user permission any time the page reloads. The hot-swap module mechanism meant that we could deploy new code without having to manually interact with each of the listening devices in turn.

From that point on my involvement was mainly to sit by the laptop chatting with Fable 5.2 about what was going on, and occasionally requesting new features. Here are some of the feature prompts I ran:

I think we need to make it so I can drag things around on the map in “rough mode”, where my job is just to put them roughly where they are, then switch out of rough mode and it attempts to get them accurate

what’s a good way for me to test this I wonder? Can we have it listen for claps, then I could clap and it could identify the location of the clap? [...]

That added the thing where any time I clapped it would show on the map as a different symbol from the beeps.

That made it easier to spot which symbol likely reflected which real-world sound.

The log should show beeps and claps with their timestamps AND have a little play button which, when clicked, replays the recorded noise from each of the listeners in sequence (with clear text on screen showing which listener recorded which snippet) while temporarily turning off microphone recording while that replay plays

Now I could replay sounds, making it much easier to identify which recorded clip was the mysterious beep I was looking for.

There should be a button next to a recording for “This is the mystery beep” - then I can hit replay to see and then confirm it was the mystery beep if that’s the one I am looking for

Then the system can categorize noises in the future to see if they are likely that same mysterious beep and use that information to build a more accurate idea of where it is

At this point I was getting close—I had a solid idea of where the beep was coming from, but wouldn’t it be neat if I could reposition the listeners around that point to get an even finer location?

I want a feature for this, I don’t want to have to restart each listening device etc, I want to be able to click a “Reposition the devices” button which lets me switch into repositioning, then I click “Repositioned” and it puts me into Rough mode and asks me to roughly locate them, then I do that and click, then it starts up again. The previous session can be read-only viewed through the app.

add a feature where the map includes a spot that is a suggestion for a location that it would be useful to add a listener at - based on data collected so far

I think the most interesting part of this project is that I demonstrated it’s possible to give Claude Code ears .

Claude doesn’t have native audio input (yet), but it can run JavaScript and Python code that can analyze audio captured by a microphone.

I told it to run a web server with WebSocket connections to multiple listening devices, then had it both run a WebAudio microphone on those devices and hook them up so they could be sent fresh JavaScript code to execute via that WebSocket.

Then I could pretty much leave Claude alone, hacking away at the problem, querying the audio logs, and reconfiguring its ears to help it solve the problem.

I’m reminded of a similar hack I heard about at GitHub Universe a few weeks ago, where Martin Woodward told me he had been debugging the GitHub Universe Badge computers by plugging them into a computer via USB-C and then pointing a webcam at their screen, so his coding agent could tell if updates were working correctly or not.
